claim.claim-text: 1. A drug delivery ocular implant (53) comprising:
2. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 1, further comprising a retention protrusion (359) extending from the second end (50) of the outer shell (54).
3. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 1, further comprising a fluid inflow pathway (38k) and a fluid outflow pathway (56k) positioned at or near the second end (50) of the outer shell (54).

4. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 3, wherein the fluid outflow pathway (56k) is configured to allow ocular fluid to be directed through the implant via the fluid inflow pathway (38k) to a physiological outflow space.
5. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 4, wherein the physiological outflow space is Schlemm's Canal.

6. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 1, wherein the cap (54a) is press fit onto the outer shell (54) and wherein the membrane (60) applies a pressure against the cap (54a) by an elastic rebound of the membrane (60).
7. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 1, further comprising the drug (62) positioned within the interior lumen (58).
8. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 7, wherein the drug (62) comprises at least one of bimatoprost, latanoprost, travoprost, or unoprostone.
9. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 1, wherein the membrane (60) seals the interior lumen (58) of the outer shell (54) from an outer environment.
10. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 1, wherein the membrane (60) defines a release rate of the drug.
11. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 1, wherein the implant (53) has a length of between about 0.5 mm and about 2.5 mm.
12. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 1, wherein the outer shell (54) and cap (54a) are manufactured separately and then assembled for insertion.
13. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 1, wherein the membrane (60) comprises ethyelene vinyl acetate.
14. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 1, wherein the membrane (60) is configured to function as a gasket and seals the interior lumen (58) from an outer environment.
15. The drug delivery ocular implant of Claim 1, wherein the membrane (60) limits fluid communication from an exterior area to the interior lumen (58).
